payload.context: A CPU executes instructions through the fetch-decode-execute cycle. In the fetch phase, the program counter identifies the memory address of the next instruction, which is loaded into the instruction register. During decoding, the control unit interprets the opcode and operands. In the execute phase, the arithmetic logic unit (ALU) performs computations or the data is moved between registers and memory. Modern CPUs use pipelining to overlap these stages, and branch prediction to speculatively execute likely code paths, improving throughput.
